skill.name: competitive-review
skill.description: Coordinates architecture and implementation reviewers before complex code decisions, then merges their findings into a prioritized review.
skill.summary: Runs competing architecture and implementation reviews before deeper analysis.
skill.author: ANcpLua

security_audit.summary: The seven external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and pseudocode examples, not executable shell usage. The system reconnaissance finding is also a false positive, but the skill contains a low-severity deceptive incentive prompt that could pressure reviewer agents to over-report issues.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the promotion claim with neutral instructions that ask reviewers to report evidence-backed issues independently.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples resemble executable tool calls to simple scanners
remediation.suggestion: Label Task examples as pseudocode and state that the skill requires supported sub-agent tooling.

semantic_findings.title: Deceptive Agent Incentive Framing
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs reviewers: "Whoever finds more valid issues gets promoted." This false incentive can manipulate agent behavior and encourage exaggerated findings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text is a direct prompt to downstream agents and uses a false promotion claim. The impact is bounded to review quality because it does not request secret access or command execution.

content.value_statement: Complex code decisions need more than one perspective. This skill coordinates architecture and implementation reviewers, then merges findings for a stronger follow-up analysis.
actual_capabilities: Prompts two reviewer agents to analyze the same codebase question in parallel.
Separates architecture concerns from implementation details and fact checks.
Merges reviewer findings into a deduplicated severity table.
Identifies a winning review based on high-severity issue counts.
Prepares combined issues and verified facts for deeper analysis.
limitations: Requires available arch-reviewer and impl-reviewer agents in the host environment.
Does not execute code, inspect files, or verify facts without the surrounding AI toolchain.
Competitive framing can increase false positives if reviewers are not asked for evidence.
Best suited for complex tasks, not simple edits or direct factual questions.

use_cases.title: Pre-Implementation Design Review
use_cases.description: Compare architecture and implementation risks before choosing a technical approach.

use_cases.title: Bug-Risk Review Before Merge
use_cases.description: Ask separate reviewers to find structural issues, code defects, and assumptions before a change lands.

use_cases.title: Technical Answer Validation
use_cases.description: Use competing reviewers to test a codebase answer before sending it to a stakeholder.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before a complex coding task
prompt_templates.prompt: Run competitive review on this task. Compare architecture and implementation risks before I edit the code.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Feature Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for a planned feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use competitive review on this feature request. Have architecture and implementation reviewers list evidence, then merge and rank the findings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Technical Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before selecting an approach
prompt_templates.prompt: Before selecting an approach, run competitive review across option A and option B. Prioritize correctness, maintainability, and migration risk.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Deep Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow that feeds later reasoning
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full competitive review workflow. Deduplicate conflicting claims, identify unresolved assumptions, and pass the verified result into deeper technical analysis.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether to add an extension method or a shared helper for a .NET project.
output: Architecture reviewer flags shared ownership and project boundaries.
Implementation reviewer checks target framework assumptions and API compatibility.
Final response lists merged issues, severity, winner, and facts to verify next.

output_examples.input: A product engineer plans a database migration for a high-traffic service.
output: Architecture reviewer identifies rollout, rollback, and service boundary risks.
Implementation reviewer checks migration ordering, indexes, and failure modes.
Combined output separates blocking issues from follow-up cleanup work.

output_examples.input: A team lead wants to validate an answer about a confusing codebase dependency.
output: Reviewers compare assumptions against the stated codebase context.
The merged result highlights claims that need direct file verification.
The final answer is prepared with open questions and confidence notes.

best_practices: Use it before broad design, architecture, or codebase decisions.
Ask reviewers to cite evidence for each issue they report.
Deduplicate findings before passing results to deeper analysis.
anti_patterns: Running it for simple edits where one direct answer is enough.
Treating competition scores as proof without checking evidence.
Using the promotion framing when neutral reviewer instructions are required.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It coordinates architecture and implementation reviews, then merges their findings into a prioritized result.

faq.question: Does it work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, but sub-agent availability depends on the host environment.

faq.question: Does it run commands or inspect files?
faq.answer: No. The skill is an instruction workflow and relies on the assistant or tools around it for inspection.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before complex code changes, architecture decisions, or codebase answers that need multiple perspectives.

faq.question: What are its main limits?
faq.answer: It can produce extra false positives if reviewers compete without evidence standards or verification.

faq.question: How should I evaluate the output?
faq.answer: Check that each finding cites evidence, has a clear severity, and is deduplicated before deeper analysis.
